hero.title: SBIBank
hero.description: Family banking with separate parent and child banking apps. Where single user can act in multiple roles within the app

meta.role: Led design team, art direction, product strategy, and core concepts
meta.scope: Discovery →  Core App MVP → Child App MVP →  Launch + Support
meta.team: Up to 5 designers: product and graphic

parts.label: Parent app
parts.text: Native iOS and Android apps separated family money from personal accounts. Blue marked shared finances and neutral marked personal ones, so owners could control family spending while each member kept their own.

parts.label: Child app
parts.text: The child app stayed savings-first: a goal-based piggy bank, tasks, and history. It taught money in small steps, and a parent could not open a child’s savings without permission.

parts.label: Full bank
parts.text: Single users still needed a complete bank, so ordering a card, payments, deposits, loans, and loyalty lived in the same product as the family roles.

beats.label: Problem
beats.text: The team had to deliver native parent and child apps, including the complete banking core, within a reduced MVP timeline.

beats.label: Research
beats.text: We prioritized essential scenarios and identified reusable patterns across accounts, cards, transactions, payments, and family features.

beats.label: Iterations
beats.text: We built a shared design foundation while adapting navigation, content, and functionality to each audience.

beats.label: Outcome
beats.text: Two connected native apps with a consistent product language, released in six months instead of the initially planned eight.

beats.label: Problem
beats.text: Parents needed to manage shared family money without mixing it with their personal accounts, while different family members required different levels of access.

beats.label: Research
beats.text: We mapped family roles, permissions, spending scenarios, and the needs of both family and single users.

beats.label: Iterations
beats.text: We separated family and personal finances through account structure, permissions, and color-coded interfaces.

beats.label: Outcome
beats.text: A clear family banking model where owners could control shared spending while each member retained access to their own finances.

beats.label: Problem
beats.text: The child app needed to teach financial responsibility without becoming too complex, restrictive, or dependent on constant parental control.

beats.label: Research
beats.text: We explored via survey how parents introduced money to children and found different needs across age groups.

beats.label: Iterations
beats.text: We designed rewarded tasks, goal-based piggy banks, child-friendly copy, and age-appropriate controls with parental approval.

beats.label: Outcome
beats.text: A savings-first experience that gave children more independence while keeping parents informed and in control.

beats.label: Problem
beats.text: The bank supported a wide range of service providers, many of which returned inconsistent or unstructured payment data.

beats.label: Research
beats.text: We analyzed key payment types, repeat-payment behavior, provider requirements, and common input patterns.

beats.label: Iterations
beats.text: We introduced adaptive local forms, autocomplete, recent-activity templates, and a consistent structure across payment and transfer flows.

beats.label: Outcome
beats.text: A scalable payment experience that supported diverse providers while remaining predictable and easy to use.
